name: Lý Sơn Island
summary: A volcanic island off the coast, famous for its garlic fields, its sea cliffs and the sailors who once travelled to the Paracel Islands.

hero.file: Mot phan quang canh Ly Son.jpg

eras.label: Long ago
eras.title: Born of volcanoes
eras.text: Lý Sơn is the top of an ancient volcano. Its craters, black rocks and sea caves were shaped by eruptions and then by the waves.

image.file: Dao Ly Son nhin tu xa.jpg
image.alt: Lý Sơn seen from the sea

eras.label: 17th–19th c.
eras.title: The Hoàng Sa sailors
eras.text: For about two hundred years, the Nguyễn lords and emperors recruited sailors from Lý Sơn for the Hoàng Sa flotilla, which sailed to the Paracel Islands each year to collect goods, map the islands and mark them.

image.file: Tau danh ca tai Ly Son.jpg

eras.label: 2000s
eras.title: Garlic island
eras.text: Farmers grow a small, strongly flavoured garlic in fields covered with white sand carried up from the beach. Lý Sơn garlic became famous across Vietnam.

eras.label: Today
eras.title: A favourite island
eras.text: Fast boats from the mainland bring visitors to see the cliffs of Hang Câu, the crater of Thới Lới and the white sands of the smaller island, Bé.

image.file: Bãi tắm đảo bé Lý Sơn.jpg

story.title: The Hoàng Sa sailors

image.file: Tau danh ca tai Ly Son.jpg

story.narration: From the 17th century, the Nguyễn rulers sent a flotilla of small boats each year from Lý Sơn to the Paracel Islands, known in Vietnamese as Hoàng Sa. The sailors collected goods from shipwrecks, caught fish and measured the islands. The voyage was dangerous, and many did not come back. Before leaving, families held a ceremony for them, the Khao lề thế lính, with small model boats and figures to take the sailors' place in death. The ceremony is still held on the island every spring.

story.title: Garlic on volcanic soil
story.narration: Lý Sơn's soil is volcanic and dry. To grow garlic, farmers spread a layer of fine white sand from the sea over the dark earth. The sand keeps moisture in and the soil cool. The garlic that grows here is small, single-cloved or with tiny cloves, and very fragrant. Island families also grow onions and other crops in the same way, and the patchwork of green fields and white sand is one of the island's most striking sights.

story.title: Cliffs and craters

image.file: Mot phan quang canh Ly Son.jpg

story.narration: On the island's north-east coast, the sea has carved the cliffs of Hang Câu, a wall of layered volcanic rock where waves pound at the foot. Inland, Thới Lới mountain is an old crater, now partly filled with a reservoir. A small temple cave, Chùa Hang, is built into the rock by the sea. At sunrise and sunset the black rocks and the blue water make the island one of the most photographed places on the central coast.

guide.price: Free to visit the island; pay for the boat from Sa Kỳ port (about 30–60 minutes).

hours.notes: An island, always open. Boats run in the daytime and may stop in rough seas.

do: Check the weather; boats are cancelled when the sea is rough.
Rent a motorbike to go around the island.
Visit the Hoàng Sa flotilla exhibition.
dont: Climb the cliffs without a guide.

tips.title: Island food
tips.text: Garlic salad, seaweed, and grilled seafood; take some garlic home.

tips.title: Getting there
tips.text: Boats leave from Sa Kỳ port, about 20 km from Quảng Ngãi city.

tips.title: Do not miss
tips.text: Hang Câu cliffs, Thới Lới crater and a boat to Bé island.
